I am a 24 year old male. My girlfriend and I have been together for over 6 1/2 years, and have been living together for over 5 years. It's also relevant to note that her sister is staying with us right now, and has been for the last 4 - 5 months. Last night, she told me that she wants to move out and get an apartment with her sister. There's some backstory to this, so I'm going to try to be succinct but explain it all.

-Like I said, we've been together for about 6 1/2 years. About 2 years ago, she came to me and told me that she was worried we wouldn't work out, and because of those doubts she was questioning the relationship and considering taking a break. We talked about it for a few days, and what ended up happening was that she went to stay with a friend for an indefinite amount of time. About a week later, we agreed to meet and talk and she told me that she really missed me and had made a mistake and wanted to come back. She moved back in, and we worked on things, and they were really good, great even, for a long time.

-In July of 2015, her sister was badly beaten by her boyfriend at the time and ended up in the hospital. He was arrested, and she was very emotionally damaged. She came to stay with us shortly thereafter. Since then, she's been experiencing massive emotional fluctuations, both because of what happened to her and other factors. She's also dealing with the court case against her ex, who was brought up on several charges for the attack.

-In September of 2015, my girlfriend told me she'd been having the same feelings she'd been having before, and worried that the week she was with her friend hadn't been enough time for her to really figure out how she felt. She talked about wanting to move out and into her own place. This wouldn't necessarily end our relationship, but we'd be taking a break at the very least and the overall tone seemed to be that it'd be over. She was, however, very conflicted about this. Throughout all of it, she made it very clear that she still loves me, she just didn't feel independent enough, felt like she relies on me too much, and wanted to see if she was capable of making it on her own.

-We talked about it at length again, and what it came down to was that it was basically over. It's also worth noting that we'd been engaged at this point - I'd proposed to her in October of 2014 and she'd said yes, though we both agreed that we wanted a longer engagement than normal to make sure it was what we wanted. She returned the ring. However, the next day when she came home from work, she was in tears and said she felt like a terrible person and she wanted to work on our relationship. We talked a lot more, and agreed that we both wanted to work on it.

-Fast forward to now. Things have been alright, but over the last couple of weeks she's seemed distant. I finally got her to tell me what's going on last night, and she told me that she's been thinking about moving out again and getting a place with her sister. Her sister is still very emotionally compromised and has been out of work for most of this time, and she said she feels like this would be a "kick in the pants" to get her on the right track.

She told me that she loves me and cares about me, but that she feels like she doesn't love me as much as she is supposed to, and that she's not a good enough girlfriend because she doesn't always compliment me. She also said that marriage is something that she wants in the future, but because of the above reasons she doesn't know if it's me she wants to marry.

My position throughout all of this has always been that I'm willing to do whatever it takes to salvage this. I love her with all of my heart, and I can't imagine being with anyone else. I told her last night that if this is really what she wants, I'm not going to try to stop her, but that I think it would be a rash decision to throw away 6 1/2 years and the deep connections we have with each other's family over what might turn out to be something we can easily solve.

I told her that I don't feel we've really done much to work on our relationship in the last 5 - 6 months, and so it doesn't really surprise me much that she feels this way. If you don't water a tree, it dies. If you don't work on a relationship, it dies. I told her that nothing in life is ever as perfect as it is in the movies, and that as long as she still loves me I feel that it's worth working on. She agreed with a lot of this, but said that she has to think about everything before any kind of decision is made.

What should I do? I want to marry this girl and have a family with her. I love her - and I love her family. At the same time though, I don't want to have to go through this whole ordeal again in 6 months, or a year, or two years. It's been extremely difficult on me emotionally - at the time of writing this I feel sick to the point where I can't even think of eating. I didn't sleep last night at all. This morning before she left for the day, she gave me a very long hug, a kiss, and told me that she loves me.
